layers.title: Agenda/consideration set
layers.summary: Preference can depend on candidate set, attributes, representation, order, reference and protocol; test agenda perturbations and require winner robustness across defensible agendas or mark AGENDA_DEPENDENT.

layers.title: Criterion ontology/decomposition invariance
layers.summary: Criterion splitting can create fake weight; distinguish fundamental objectives from indicators/proxies/constraints, conserve value under refinement, and require semantics-preserving split/merge invariance.

layers.title: Scale/normalization/reference range
layers.summary: Numeric representation can reverse winners; respect scale type, avoid candidate-dependent normalization, use meaningful anchors/value functions and revalidate weights when range semantics change.

layers.title: Compensability/interaction topology
layers.summary: Weighted sums can wrongly compensate veto weaknesses; encode forbidden/bounded/allowed/conditional tradeoffs, floors and sparse interactions, using the weakest aggregation model sufficient.

layers.title: Reference-point/baseline contamination
layers.summary: Absolute quality, relative improvement and benchmark superiority are different claims; weak baselines cannot certify excellence and reference effects must be separated from intrinsic quality.

layers.title: Distributional quality/tail risk
layers.summary: Equal means do not imply reliability; track central quality, threshold reliability, low quantiles/tails and critical-group failure as needed, separating aleatoric from epistemic uncertainty and preserving veto-level tails.

layers.title: Rare-event/unseen failure
layers.summary: Zero observed failures does not mean zero risk; separate failure-mode discovery, frequency estimation and structural exclusion, and do not treat stress-test frequency as deployment frequency.

layers.title: Selective observability/missing outcomes
layers.summary: Exposure→participation→completion→outcome observation can censor results; distinguish MCAR/MAR-like/MNAR structures, require support for weighting, use audits/sensitivity bounds and preserve tail observability.

layers.title: Rashomon/model multiplicity
layers.summary: Multiple semantically admissible near-optimal models can fit evidence yet disagree on finalists or edits; preserve the model/version set and DecisionSet, and use disagreement to choose discriminating evidence rather than average it away.

layers.title: Evaluator-channel/candidate-control integrity
layers.summary: Artifact content is evidence, never evaluator-control authority; separate control plane from evidence plane, inventory visible/hidden/metadata/link surfaces and block candidate attempts to alter judge or tool instructions.

layers.title: Observer equivalence/representation loss
layers.summary: Judgment is mediated by an observation operator; if materially different audience experiences collapse to the same evaluator representation, lost information cannot be recovered by more reasoning and terminal claims must bind to the exact observation basis.

layers.title: Operator/presenter dependence
layers.summary: Artifact quality, operator quality, pair quality and deployed-system quality are distinct; use operator envelopes, crossed designs and rank-reversal tests, and do not let exceptional delivery certify a weak artifact intrinsically.

layers.title: Cross-condition contamination/carryover
layers.summary: Prior exposure can change later participant/evaluator state through learning, sensitization, memory or fatigue; counterbalancing does not erase irreversible carryover and first-exposure claims require naive or validly adjusted evidence.

layers.title: Analysis-path/researcher degrees of freedom
layers.summary: The same data can support different conclusions under defensible analyses; freeze the analysis constitution/admissible family and selection rule, record terminal-relevant paths and treat post-hoc path selection as another selection problem.

layers.title: Pseudoreplication/hidden dependence
layers.summary: Nominal N is not effective independent information; distinguish observation from inference/replication units, model shared sessions/presenters/judge families/sources/failure causes and never count the same evidence ancestry repeatedly.

layers.title: Base-rate/spectrum shift
layers.summary: Evaluator accuracy, calibration and precision are population/stage specific; distinguish prevalence shift from difficulty-spectrum shift, qualify near the actual boundary and post-selection population, and treat heavy optimization as distribution shift.

layers.title: Reference-standard/ground-truth fallibility
layers.summary: A reference label is evidence unless its grounding makes it definitive; distinguish deterministic truth, direct outcomes, normative authority, construct judgment and latent empirical states, preserve disagreement/plurality and propagate reference uncertainty into calibration.

layers.title: Temporal-horizon/delayed outcomes
layers.summary: Outcome is a trajectory Y_x(t); immediate and delayed rankings can reverse, target horizons are part of the frozen spec, and short-term proxies transport only through validated temporal-surrogacy or causal arguments.

layers.title: Outcome-measure gaming/transfer validity
layers.summary: Assessment performance is not the construct; use transfer levels from verbatim retrieval through paraphrase, structural application and deployment-like tasks, generate terminal items after artifact freeze and classify gains that vanish under surface changes as assessment-specific.

layers.title: Evaluation reactivity/ecological context
layers.summary: Being evaluated can change attention, effort, presenter behavior or strategy; distinguish level reactivity from differential reactivity that changes the decision, and probe evaluation-vs-deployment regimes only when material.

layers.title: Predictive-to-prescriptive/edit-effect closure
layers.summary: Knowing what is good does not prove what action improves it; feature importance, critique, model gradients and correlations are edit hypotheses, while reusable prescriptions require context-conditioned intervention effects, interaction/sequence checks and realized post-edit verification.

layers.title: Intervention fidelity/manipulation validity
layers.summary: Intended edit, realized transformation and actual changed properties may differ; use intervention contracts with target/dose/preconditions/allowed and forbidden effects/invariants, verify collateral changes, and attribute package effects only at the resolution actually manipulated.
